rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The theme that tests our vocabulary and our ethics Animals are the theme where description and conscience share a leash: the same paragraph must name the creature precisely and decide how we owe it. Nepal makes the theme vivid — tigers and rhinos are a census success story here, elephants occasionally attend village meetings uninvited, and every monsoon the streets fill with somebody's abandoned puppies.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Animal rights vs human use — present both positions before your own.
Note personification of animals in texts and what it reveals about humans.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ## The debates, held honestly **"Zoos: prisons or sanctuaries?"** Concede the cage's indictment — pacing predators, concrete enclosures. Rebut with the modern zoo's changed job: breeding programmes for the near-extinct, veterinary care, the child who sees a tiger and grows up to fund its forest.…  ·  ## Grammar and style: comparison and habit Animals invite **comparison**, and the grammar must keep up: "A cheetah runs **faster than** a deer"; "The rhino is **the most heavily built** of them all"; "A cat sleeps **as much as** sixteen hours a day". Watch the double comparatives ("more faster" — the classic slip) and the irregulars (*good/better/best, bad/worse/worst*) that examiners salt into every paper.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## How the exam asks it The **descriptive essay** ("The animal I like most", 6–8 marks) wants one animal, seen precisely: appearance in naturalist detail, habitat and habits in the present simple, one reason for your choice that is not "it is beautiful". rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Why should humans protect animal habitats? (2 marks) — biodiversity and ecosystem balance; human survival depends on it.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The words that carry the theme Precision begins with the **collective nouns** the exam loves: a **pack** of wolves, a **herd** of elephants, a **flock** of birds, a **swarm** of bees, a **pride** of lions, a **school** of fish. Then the family words: **cub, calf, kitten, chick, foal, puppy**; and the gender pairs the paper tests — **lion/lioness, tiger/tigress, bull/cow, ram/ewe, stallion/mare**.…  ·  ## Reading the theme like a writer — the devices animals carry **Personification** is the theme's oldest device — animals in literature think, plot and judge because it lets writers say human things at a safe distance: the crow's persistence in the fable is really a lecture on patience.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Animal texts often argue ethics — organise answers as welfare facts (sentience, suffering) + human duty + one practice to change.  ·  Trick 2: Comprehension questions target behaviour details (habitat, diet, instinct) — underline them during reading.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. Is keeping animals in zoos justified? (2 marks) — conservation and education vs captivity stress; end with conditions that justify it.
